html:
Bundelkhand is a hilly region of central India, split today between Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, named after the Bundela Rajputs who ruled it from the 1500s. On the 1800 map its shape stretches much further east than the real region.

In earlier times this was the land of the Chandelas, builders of the Khajuraho temples. The Bundelas made Orchha their capital in 1531. In the 1600s Chhatrasal rebelled against Aurangzeb and founded his own kingdom. In 1729, under attack by a Mughal governor, he called for help from the Maratha general Baji Rao I, and gave him a third of his land in thanks.

By 1800 Bundelkhand was a patchwork of small Bundela states and Maratha holdings such as Jhansi, all under pressure from the Marathas and the British. After the Treaty of Bassein in 1802 the British took control. In 1857 Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi fought them here.
sum: Bundelkhand is a hilly region of central India, split today between Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, named after the Bundela Rajputs who ruled it from the 1500s. On the 1800 map its shape stretches much further east than the real region.
